verses.text: Wine makes a mockery of people, and beer gets them brawling. Let either one lead you off course and you're acting without wisdom.
A king can strike terror like a roaring lion. Make him furious and you're risking your life.
There's honor in staying out of a fight. Any fool can find something to argue about.
A lazy person won't plow because it's cold. Come harvest, they'll be begging and come away with nothing.
Advice can sit deep in someone's heart like water in a well. A person with understanding knows how to draw it out.
Plenty of people say their love never quits. But who can find somebody who actually stays faithful?
A person who does right walks with integrity. Their children are blessed after them.
When a king sits on his judgment throne, one look from him scatters evil.
Who can honestly say, “I've made my heart pure. I'm clean and haven't sinned”?
Using one set of weights for buying and another for selling, or doing the same with measures, disgusts the LORD either way.
Even kids show who they are by what they do, whether their actions are clean and right.
Ears that hear and eyes that see, the LORD made both.
Don't love sleep so much that you end up poor. Open your eyes and you'll have bread enough to eat.
“This isn't worth much. It's junk,” says the buyer. Then they walk away bragging about the deal they got.
There's gold, and there are plenty of rubies. Someone who speaks with knowledge is a rare jewel.
Take the coat of someone who guarantees a stranger's debt. Hold it as security when they've put themselves on the line for a woman who strays.
Food you got by cheating tastes sweet at first. Later your mouth is full of gravel.
Get advice to make your plans solid. Go to war with wise guidance.
People who go around spreading stories give away secrets. Keep your distance from somebody who can't keep their mouth shut.
Curse your father or mother and your lamp will go out in pitch darkness.
An inheritance you grab too fast at the start won't come with a blessing at the end.
Don't say, “I'll make them pay for what they did.” Wait for the LORD. He'll save you.
The LORD hates dishonest weights. Rigged scales don't please him.
The LORD directs your steps. How can you expect to understand the whole road yourself?
You're setting a trap for yourself when you promise something to God in a rush and only think about the vow later.
A wise king separates out the wicked and rolls the threshing wheel over them.
Your spirit is the LORD's lamp. It shines into the deepest parts of you.
Love and faithfulness keep a king safe. Love keeps his throne standing.
Young men can take pride in their strength. Gray hair is what gives older men their splendor.
Blows that leave wounds can scrub away evil. Beatings can reach all the way to what hides inside.
